correctness.rationale: For the Fiedler eigenspace E of the core, vertex transitivity makes its projector diagonal constant and edge transitivity makes the averaged squared core-edge displacement 2k*lambda_2/(nd). Lifting each normalized Fiedler eigenvector to leaves with factor 1+t, t=sqrt(lambda_2/d), gives an averaged positive Laplacian Rayleigh quotient equal to (a/(nD))(2 sum_core_edges w+sum_pendants q) <= a/D=alpha by core stochastic budgets; min-max forces spectral SLEM >=1-alpha even without invariant weights. The explicit p*=(1+r(1+t))/(dD), q*=t(1+t)/D satisfies dp*+rq*=1. The 2x2 Laplacian mode blocks over all base Laplacian eigenvalues attain smallest positive alpha; trace and rho_max<=2d bound the largest Laplacian eigenvalue by 2-alpha, controlling the negative Markov eigenvalues. Equality saturates every core budget and makes every lifted Fiedler vector an alpha-eigenvector; positive Fiedler-projector diagonal forces each individual leaf q to q* even for non-invariant optima. Direct independent full-matrix eigenvalue checks on C4,C5,K4,Petersen for r=1,2,3 agreed numerically. Finite spectra corroborate rather than prove global optimum.
residual_risks: Symmetry of transition matrix, nonnegative entries, stochastic row budgets and both vertex/edge transitivity are essential; no uniqueness for noninvariant core-edge weights is asserted.

value.rationale: An exact fastest-mixing spectral constant for an infinite natural family of leaf-corona graphs, valid against all non-invariant symmetric stochastic kernels, is a meaningful optimization theorem. The new local uniqueness of pendant transitions among all global optima identifies structurally forced conductances; the result extends and sharpens previously known special cores, not just the standard SDP formulation.
residual_risks: The theorem does not optimize nonreversible chains or finite-time total-variation mixing, nor prove all noninvariant core edges unique.

final_claim: For every connected finite vertex- and edge-transitive d-regular core H of order n>=3, d>=2, with r>=1 private leaves per core vertex, the minimum SLEM of a symmetric nonnegative stochastic transition matrix supported on its leaf corona is exactly 1-a/[1+r(1+sqrt a)^2], a=lambda_2(L_H)/d. The stated uniform core and leaf edge probabilities attain it, and every unrestricted global optimum has exactly those leaf probabilities and zero core holding.
limitations: Requires connected simple vertex- and edge-transitive regular H, symmetric row-stochastic nonnegative kernels; does not assert uniqueness of unrestricted core-edge weights. Small-graph numeric verification not a proof of global optimality.
